2026-11-06.headline: SAF maps Zero Trust frameworks to disciplines, roles, capabilities, and implementation
2026-11-06.overview: The period centered on a substantive expansion and reorganization of Microsoft’s Security Adoption Framework guidance. New mapping guidance covers Zero Trust, the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, and the DoD Zero Trust Strategy, while related SAF material adds connections among business priorities, risk, responsibilities, implementation, and measurement. Two lower-impact updates refreshed titles and publication dates for MCRA and the SecOps workshop.
2026-11-06.adminImpact: Security architects and administrators can use the new framework mappings and role- or objective-based navigation to plan security improvements, coordinate stakeholders, assess alignment, and direct teams to relevant guidance. No configuration, migration, or other operational change is specified; the MCRA and SecOps updates primarily improve identification of current guidance.

keyChanges.title: New standards-to-SAF mappings
keyChanges.detail: The new guidance maps security standards and framework objectives to SAF disciplines, roles, Microsoft security capabilities, and implementation guidance, including mappings for Zero Trust, the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, and the DoD Zero Trust Strategy.

keyChanges.title: SAF now links strategy through measurement
keyChanges.detail: The SAF page now connects business priorities, risk, Zero Trust principles, security disciplines, technologies, and technical solutions, and adds guidance on shared responsibilities, implementation, measurement, and four connected framework components across hybrid, multicloud, and multiplatform environments.

keyChanges.title: SAF navigation shifts to goals and roles
keyChanges.detail: “Using SAF effectively” now directs readers through tables organized around objectives and organizational roles, linking to strategy, architecture, disciplines, scenarios, technologies, workshops, and related guidance instead of the former top-down, build-up, and scenario-driven patterns.

keyChanges.title: MCRA title and publication date refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The MCRA page and heading now omit “Review,” and its publication date is shown as November 6, 2026, replacing November 2.

keyChanges.title: SecOps workshop naming and date updated
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Zero Trust Workshop page now uses “SecOps” capitalization in its title and heading, and its page date changed from May 24 to November 6, 2026.

2026-11-08.headline: SAF maps established security guidance into integrated, aligned, and companion resources
2026-11-08.overview: A new Security Adoption Framework (SAF) article explains how existing Microsoft security guidance relates to SAF. It groups resources as integrated, SAF-aligned, or companion guidance and maps them to SAF disciplines.
2026-11-08.adminImpact: Administrators can use the mappings to locate relevant planning, architecture, implementation, and operations guidance. No administrative action is specified.

keyChanges.title: SAF guidance mapping
keyChanges.detail: The article organizes established Microsoft security resources into integrated, SAF-aligned, and companion categories, with mappings to SAF disciplines and related planning, architecture, implementation, and operations guidance.

2026-11-15.headline: AI security, post-quantum readiness, and assessments gain new SAF guidance
2026-11-15.overview: The most consequential additions put concrete planning structure around the Security Adoption Framework (SAF): seven AI security control areas, cryptographic dependency discovery and quantum-resistant migration planning, and a documented workflow for reviewing Zero Trust Assessment results. Related pages map CIS Controls and Benchmarks, NIST CSF 2.0, and The Open Group Zero Trust model to SAF roles, disciplines, technologies, and implementation guidance. Updated Secure Future Initiative material emphasizes phishing-resistant authentication, managed identities, and secret and key lifecycle protection, while SecOps guidance adds incident governance, human oversight, and four implementation patterns.
2026-11-15.adminImpact: Use the new SAF material to sequence AI inventories, lifecycle governance, least-privilege and monitoring work; discover cryptographic dependencies and plan phased post-quantum replacements; and investigate skipped or errored assessment checks before optionally importing mapped findings into Zero Trust Workshop notes. Apply the standards mappings to assign owners and establish configuration baselines, and review SFI identity and secret priorities against existing privileged-access and key-management practices.

keyChanges.title: AI security guidance defines seven control areas
keyChanges.detail: The new Secure AI with Zero Trust guidance covers AI applications, agents, identities, models, data, tools, and infrastructure. Its seven control areas span risk assessment and access control through monitoring and response, providing scope for AI inventories, lifecycle governance, least-privilege access, data protection, secure deployment, and activity monitoring.

keyChanges.title: Post-quantum guidance starts with cryptographic dependency discovery
keyChanges.detail: New SAF guidance calls for identifying vulnerable cryptographic dependencies, planning quantum-resistant replacements, and maintaining readiness as standards and threats evolve. It addresses identity, applications, infrastructure, communications, IoT and OT, and supply-chain integrations, including harvest-now, decrypt-later exposure.

keyChanges.title: Zero Trust assessment guidance documents review and handoff steps
keyChanges.detail: The new page explains how to review reports across seven Zero Trust pillars, investigate skipped checks and errors, and optionally import mapped findings into Zero Trust Workshop task notes. It also documents report paths, prerequisites, data protections, and integration limitations.

keyChanges.title: CIS mapping separates practice prioritization from configuration baselines
keyChanges.detail: The new mapping distinguishes CIS Controls v8.1, used to prioritize security practices, from CIS Benchmarks, used for technology-specific configuration. It maps both to SAF roles, disciplines, technologies, and implementation guidance.

keyChanges.title: SFI identity guidance emphasizes phishing-resistant authentication and secret lifecycle
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance reframes identity and secret protection around reducing identity compromise, token abuse, and exposed-secret risk. It highlights phishing-resistant authentication, fewer static credentials, managed identities, automated key and secret lifecycle controls, standardized SDKs, and faster credential remediation.

2026-11-16.headline: AI-era security guidance now centers on foundations, defensive agents, and agentic insiders
2026-11-16.overview: The Zero Trust page “Security for the AI era” was retitled and substantially revised. It now addresses AI-amplified exposure, autonomous attacks, and agentic-insider risk through three priorities: secure foundations, defend with agents, and secure the agentic insider.
2026-11-16.adminImpact: Administrators should use the revised guidance to align security planning with AI-related risks and the three stated priorities. The page also contains updated links and metadata.

keyChanges.title: Revised guidance introduces three AI-security priorities
keyChanges.detail: The retitled page now explains AI-amplified exposure, autonomous attacks, and agentic-insider risk, organizing its guidance around secure foundations, defend with agents, and secure the agentic insider.

2026-11-18.headline: New SAF guidance maps Secure Future Initiative priorities to security disciplines
2026-11-18.overview: A new Zero Trust guidance page explains how Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative informs Security Adoption Framework guidance, linking SFI culture, governance, security principles, engineering priorities, and implementation practices to relevant SAF security disciplines.
2026-11-18.adminImpact: Administrators can use the mappings to support security modernization planning and adapt practices to their organization’s risks, governance, and technology environment. No required administrator action is stated.

keyChanges.title: SFI-to-SAF mapping guidance added
keyChanges.detail: The guidance connects Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative with Security Adoption Framework guidance and maps SFI areas—including culture, governance, security principles, engineering priorities, and implementation practices—to relevant SAF security disciplines.

2026-11-19.headline: Zero Trust guidance reframes foundations and agent oversight for AI-driven exposure
2026-11-19.overview: Two Zero Trust fundamentals pages were updated to center AI-amplified exposure, increasingly autonomous attacks, and the security dependencies of AI systems. The changes strengthen guidance on agent oversight, guardrails, accountability, visibility, governance, and continuous improvement.
2026-11-19.adminImpact: Security architects and administrators should use the revised priorities and expected outcomes to review AI-related assets, dependencies, identities, data, applications, infrastructure, endpoints, operations, ownership, and guardrails. The updated resources can also inform AI security planning and playbook design.

keyChanges.title: Overview adds agent-focused security priorities
keyChanges.detail: The Overview now frames agents as potential insiders and emphasizes AI-amplified exposure and increasingly autonomous attacks. It adds guidance on guardrails, playbooks, and accountability, links to Microsoft Perception, and updates its SAF reference.

keyChanges.title: Secure your foundations expands the AI readiness model
keyChanges.detail: The foundations guidance is reframed around securing the identities, data, applications, infrastructure, networks, endpoints, and operations that AI depends on. It adds expected outcomes covering visibility, data protection, identity governance, approved development practices, exposure measurement, risk ownership, and continuous improvement.

2026-11-02.headline: Security Adoption Framework guidance adds standards mappings and role-based entry points
2026-11-02.overview: The week’s substantive work centers on Security Adoption Framework (SAF) guidance: a new mapping for Zero Trust and other frameworks, a new article showing how existing Microsoft guidance fits SAF, and expanded explanations of SAF structure and navigation. The two remaining edits only changed MCRA title/date metadata and SecOps capitalization/date metadata.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Security leaders and administrators can use the expanded SAF material to map framework objectives to disciplines, roles, Microsoft capabilities, implementation guidance, and related resources; route stakeholders by objective or role; clarify shared responsibilities; and track progress across hybrid, multicloud, and multiplatform environments. The evidence identifies no configuration, migration, or other administrative change.

keyChanges.title: Framework mappings connect standards objectives to SAF execution
keyChanges.detail: New guidance maps security standards and framework objectives to SAF disciplines, roles, Microsoft security capabilities, and implementation guidance. It specifically covers Zero Trust, the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, and the DoD Zero Trust Strategy, giving administrators a basis for planning improvements, coordinating teams, and assessing alignment.

keyChanges.title: Existing Microsoft guidance is organized around SAF relationships
keyChanges.detail: A new article classifies established Microsoft security guidance as integrated, SAF-aligned, or companion guidance and maps those resources to SAF disciplines. Administrators can use it to locate planning, architecture, implementation, and operations material.

keyChanges.title: SAF now ties priorities, risk, responsibilities, and measurement together
keyChanges.detail: The SAF page now explains connections among business priorities, risk, Zero Trust principles, security disciplines, technologies, and technical solutions. It also adds guidance on shared responsibilities, implementation, measurement, and four connected framework components for hybrid, multicloud, and multiplatform environments.

keyChanges.title: SAF navigation shifts to objective- and role-based entry points
keyChanges.detail: “Using SAF effectively” replaces the previous top-down, build-up, and scenario-driven patterns with tables organized around objectives and organizational roles. The tables link readers to strategy, architecture, disciplines, scenarios, technologies, workshops, and related guidance; no configuration or migration is required.

2026-11-09.headline: New SAF guidance targets AI controls, DevSecOps, and post-quantum readiness
2026-11-09.overview: The period brought a broad Security Adoption Framework (SAF) and Zero Trust guidance expansion. New material provides planning paths for securing AI systems, governing agent-assisted defense, protecting software delivery, preparing for cryptographic migration, and relating established frameworks to SAF. Existing Secure Future Initiative and SecOps guidance was also reorganized around outcomes, governance, decision authority, and operational lifecycles.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Security architects and administrators can use the new SAF material to build AI inventories and control plans, define agent-automation boundaries, prioritize development-security backlogs, identify cryptographic dependencies, and map compliance or security practices to accountable teams and implementation work.

keyChanges.title: SAF adds seven-area guidance for securing AI environments
keyChanges.detail: The new Secure AI with Zero Trust guidance covers AI applications, agents, identities, models, data, tools, and infrastructure across seven control areas, including risk assessment, access control, monitoring, and response. It gives administrators a planning basis for AI inventories, lifecycle governance, least-privilege access, data protection, secure deployment, and activity monitoring.

keyChanges.title: Agent-assisted defense guidance defines governance and oversight practices
keyChanges.detail: Defend with agents using SAF explains how to apply AI-assisted and agentic capabilities in security operations, with emphasis on governance, human oversight, bounded automation, measurable outcomes, and SAF-aligned implementation paths. Administrators can use it to set approval and rollback boundaries, assign accountability, and measure operational effectiveness.

keyChanges.title: The DevSecOps workshop adds roadmap outputs and implementation areas
keyChanges.detail: The new Microsoft Zero Trust Workshop - DevSecOps aligns the workshop pillar with the SAF Development Security discipline and identifies roadmap outputs covering repository governance, developer access, secrets, and code review. Administrators can use the material to identify gaps and prioritize a development-security implementation backlog.

keyChanges.title: SAF introduces a post-quantum readiness planning path
keyChanges.detail: Plan cryptographic agility and post-quantum readiness directs teams to identify vulnerable cryptographic dependencies and plan quantum-resistant replacements across identity, applications, infrastructure, communications, IoT/OT, and supply-chain integrations. The guidance supports phased planning where migration requires significant lead time and sensitive data faces harvest-now, decrypt-later risk.

keyChanges.title: CIS Controls and Benchmarks receive distinct SAF mappings
keyChanges.detail: The new mapping distinguishes CIS Controls v8.1, which prioritizes security practices, from CIS Benchmarks, which provide technology-specific configuration guidance. Both are mapped to SAF roles, disciplines, technologies, and implementation guidance, giving administrators a basis for assigning ownership, establishing baselines, validating compatibility, managing exceptions, and tracking improvements.

2026-11-16.headline: Zero Trust guidance centers AI security on foundations, agents, and agentic insiders
2026-11-16.overview: This week brought a coordinated refresh of Zero Trust guidance for AI-era security. The “Security for the AI era” page now organizes the guidance around three priorities—secure foundations, defend with agents, and secure the agentic insider—while related pages expand the treatment of AI-amplified exposure, autonomous attacks, guardrails, accountability, and AI-dependent assets. A new page also maps Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative to Security Adoption Framework guidance.
2026-11-16.adminImpact: Security architects and administrators can use the revised priorities, expanded readiness outcomes, and SFI-to-SAF mappings to shape AI security planning, agent oversight, governance, and modernization work. The supplied guidance states no required administrator action.

keyChanges.title: AI-era guidance adopts three security priorities
keyChanges.detail: The retitled and substantially revised “Security for the AI era” guidance now focuses on AI-amplified exposure, autonomous attacks, and agentic-insider risk through three priorities: secure foundations, defend with agents, and secure the agentic insider. Links and metadata were also updated.

keyChanges.title: Zero Trust overview adds AI guardrails and agent accountability
keyChanges.detail: The overview now emphasizes AI-amplified exposure, increasingly autonomous attacks, and agents as insiders. It adds guidance on guardrails, playbooks, and accountability, links to Microsoft Perception, and updates its Security Adoption Framework reference.

keyChanges.title: Foundation guidance expands outcomes for AI-dependent environments
keyChanges.detail: “Secure your foundations” is now framed around protecting the identities, data, applications, infrastructure, networks, endpoints, and operations that AI depends on. It adds expected outcomes covering visibility, data protection, identity governance, approved development practices, exposure measurement, risk ownership, and continuous improvement.

keyChanges.title: New SFI guidance maps initiative areas to SAF disciplines
keyChanges.detail: The new page explains how Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative informs Security Adoption Framework guidance through culture, governance, security principles, engineering priorities, and implementation practices, and maps SFI areas to relevant SAF security disciplines.

2026-11.headline: SAF expands AI security, agent oversight, DevSecOps, and post-quantum planning
2026-11.overview: November’s substantive security guidance expansion puts AI systems, agentic operations, software delivery, and cryptographic migration into a common Security Adoption Framework (SAF) planning path. New Zero Trust material defines seven AI control areas and bounded-agent practices, while new DevSecOps and post-quantum pages add implementation and dependency-planning routes. Updated Secure Future Initiative guidance sharpens identity and secrets priorities around phishing-resistant authentication, managed identities, lifecycle automation, and exposed-secret remediation.
2026-11.adminImpact: Administrators can turn this material into four workstreams: inventory AI systems and cryptographic dependencies; define agent approval, rollback, and accountability boundaries; assess the developer-to-production path; and review phishing resistance, managed identities, secret rotation, and exposed-secret detection.

keyChanges.title: Zero Trust adds a seven-area control model for securing AI
keyChanges.detail: New guidance covers securing AI applications, agents, identities, models, data, tools, and infrastructure across seven control areas, from risk assessment and access control through monitoring and response. Administrators gain a basis for AI inventories, lifecycle governance, least-privilege design, data protection, secure deployment, and activity monitoring.

keyChanges.title: SAF defines governance boundaries for agent-assisted security operations
keyChanges.detail: The new conceptual page for AI-assisted and agentic security operations adds governance, human oversight, bounded automation, measurable outcomes, and SAF-aligned implementation paths. Security teams can use it to structure workflows, assign accountability, and define approval and rollback boundaries.

keyChanges.title: Post-quantum guidance starts with cryptographic dependency discovery
keyChanges.detail: New SAF guidance covers identifying vulnerable cryptographic dependencies, planning quantum-resistant replacements, and maintaining readiness as standards and threats evolve across identity, applications, infrastructure, communications, IoT/OT, and supply-chain integrations. It supports dependency discovery and phased planning where migration lead times and harvest-now, decrypt-later risk matter.

keyChanges.title: The DevSecOps workshop turns software-delivery gaps into a backlog
keyChanges.detail: New Zero Trust Workshop guidance aligns the DevSecOps pillar with SAF’s Development Security discipline, defines expected roadmap outputs, and focuses implementation on repository governance, developer access, secrets, and code review. Administrators can use it to identify gaps and prioritize an implementation backlog.

keyChanges.title: SFI identity guidance prioritizes phishing resistance and secret lifecycle controls
keyChanges.detail: Updated Secure Future Initiative guidance centers on reducing identity compromise, token abuse, and exposed-secret risk. Its priorities include phishing-resistant authentication, reduced static credentials through managed identities, automated key and secret lifecycle controls, standardized SDKs, and faster credential remediation. Administrators can use it to review privileged-access, credential, secret, and key-management practices.
